newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran offering fuel oil ex-Bandar Abbas - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran offering fuel oil ex-Bandar Abbas - MEES.

text.p: National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) has begun to offer fuel oil export cargoes from its new Bandar Abbas oil refinery after testing of one of the plant's two crude distillation units (CDU), the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported on Monday.
MEES quoted Iranian sources as saying NIOC had tested one of the two 116,000 barrels per day (bpd) CDUs since late June and that rates were now running at 70,000 bpd.

"NIOC has also been offering out the first export cargoes from the refinery, with load dates as from next month. Only fuel oil cargoes have been mooted...as the refinery is not producing on-spec gasoline and gas oil yet," MEES reported.
"Full start-up of the plant is likely to be still some time off however given continued problems with the sea water cooling system at the site."
Iran Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh told reporters at an OPEC meeting in June that full capacity would be reached by September after commissioning in July.
Traders expected NIOC to export no more than three or four fuel cargoes each of a maximum of 30,000 tonnes, MEES said.
"This size of cargo is suitable for the Fujairah bunker market, but it is unlikely to appeal to companies looking for long-haul opportunities," Cyprus-based MEES reported.
The second CDU is expected on stream in March 1998.
Banbar Abbas is Iran's eighth refinery and cost $2 billion.
